verdicts.strongest_argument: The finding supplies its own evidence that the pre-release was priced: it reports the 08-31 disclosure moving the stock +2.85% on 10.95m shares against a 6.20m average, and quote.json confirms 17.87 (08-28) to 18.38 (08-31) on 10.95m and then 11.75m on 09-01 - a two-day, 1.8x-volume event on exactly the date the item 2.02 8-K was accepted. So the numbers hit the tape and the tape absorbed them. What remains is the inference that the 09-08 release therefore has little surprise capacity, and that inference is drawn out inside the admissible corpus rather than left implicit: the 2026-09-07 sweep's digest (docs/41a4a7aa3d67072d0008eff3edfb23de89ebd9b6.txt) carries a 2026-09-06T11:55:53Z post titled 'GME Kills the VWAP early, Q2 prelim results, my trading position update & GME current Fair Value Update', i.e. retail was publishing fair-value work off the preliminary Q2 numbers two days ahead, and the surrounding posts in the same digest frame the print as needing non-financial news ('it's monday and there's no buyout announcement', 'we need news this week'). That is the hunter's own conclusion, published, before the print. A pre-release bundled with item 1.01 and item 3.02 is also the standard mechanics of disclosing results alongside a securities offering, which makes it structural rather than a discovery. The residual +7.2% over the five sessions after 08-31 is the only genuinely unexplained thing here, and it is at least as consistent with the offering pricing clearing and warrant speculation - both of which the same digest discusses - as with the market failing to notice a pre-release it had just traded 22m shares on.

prior_publication.what_it_says: The 8-K accepted 2026-08-31T06:23:08Z carries item 2.02, results of operations, alongside items 1.01, 3.02, 7.01 and 9.01 - the pre-release is on the public record eight days before the scheduled print.
A retail post titled 'GME Kills the VWAP early, Q2 prelim results... GME current Fair Value Update' shows the preliminary Q2 figures already being modelled two days before the print.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: quote.json, bmo name and clean-view/GME.json excludes the 2026-09-08 bar, so my last admissible close is 19.16 on 09-04. The 8-K date itself is the volume event: 10,945,600 shares on 08-31 and 11,751,300 on 09-01 against avg_volume_20d of 6,203,575, with +2.85% then +2.34%. baselines/GME.json is explicitly tier 'thin' with history_usable 0 and event_plausibility 'suspect' (8 days against a 91-day cadence), so the 4.79% median reaction it quotes is not a sound statement of what was priced - which cuts both ways and is why I am not higher than 75.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: The body of the 08-31 8-K showing the item 2.02 exhibit was something other than preliminary Q2 results - a segment restatement, say - which would leave the 09-08 release with full surprise capacity after all.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The claim states 'the tape shows no distinct de-rating on either date, which is what I would expect to see if the dilution had been separately priced', and quote.json contradicts that on the very date the finding is built on. GME closed 21.72 on 07-31 and 19.06 on 08-03 - the session of the 8-K accepted 2026-08-03T10:12:28Z carrying items 1.01/3.02/8.01/9.01 - a -12.25% single-day fall on 41,713,200 shares against a 6.20m 20-day average. That is 6.7x volume and the largest bar in the entire file; it is the de-rating the finding says is absent, and it happened on the acceptance date. The claim is therefore not merely priced, it is empirically wrong as stated. The second item 3.02, on 08-31, moved the stock the other way (+2.85%) on 1.8x volume, which is what happens when an offering prices into a bid. Beyond the bars, serial dilution is the single most-discussed feature of this capital structure in the admissible retail copy: the 2026-08-30 digest (docs/6de4101fccd1ca15af0d53df2b30801d670015a4.txt) contains 'will he do another bond dilution for the rest of the 0% interest bonds' dated 2026-08-28 and a same-day note that Robinhood's borrow rate for GME warrants rose 14%. Age is not novelty, and a rate of issuance that the holder base is openly forecasting is not an unpriced fact. The hunter also concedes the 08-31 8-K is shared with GME#0, leaving only the 08-03 filing as additional - and that is the one the tape demolishes.

prior_publication.what_it_says: 8-K items 1.01/3.02/8.01/9.01 accepted 2026-08-03T10:12:28Z - the unregistered equity sale, on the public record the morning of the -12.25% session.
Holders openly anticipate 'another bond dilution for the rest of the 0% interest bonds' and report a 14% jump in the warrant borrow rate - the dilution risk is the consensus frame, not a hidden one.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: quote.json: 07-31 close 21.72, 08-03 close 19.06 (-12.25%) on 41.7m shares versus a 6.2m 20d average; 08-31 close 18.38 (+2.85%) on 10.9m. Both item 3.02 dates carry outsized volume, so neither issuance passed unpriced. Spot 19.16 on the last admissible bar sits 30.81% below the 52-week high and 7.22% above the low, i.e. the de-rating the finding wants to predict has already happened.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A dated disclosure of shares actually issued under the two item 3.02 events large enough that the diluted share count used in consensus EPS is materially stale, rather than an inference from item codes.

interactions: Both findings rest on the same 2026-08-31 8-K, which the hunter states outright and asks to be collapsed into one source cluster; only the 2026-08-03 8-K is additional, and that is the document whose own price bar refutes GME#1. GME#0 also depends on the 08-31 filing being a genuine pre-release, so if that were wrong both claims would move together.
